title: The Lost Child
text: A child sits on a stone by the road, crying quietly into her sleeve. She wears a smock and bonnet from a town that burned a hundred years ago, and there is soot on her cheeks. She has not grown up at all, and does not seem to know it.

options.label: Take the child along; no one should be left alone out here.

outcomes.text: She walks with you as far as the next bend, smiles, and is gone. The air smells of bread and smoke.
The child is not a child. It has been waiting for someone kind.

options.label: The sharpest asks her a few gentle questions before anyone takes her hand.

outcomes.text: Her answers are wrong in small ways. Those small wrongs tell you a great deal about what lives here.

options.label: Leave her on her stone. Whatever she is, she has waited a hundred years already.

outcomes.text: The crying follows you for hours. When it stops, the silence is worse.
